The mentor rule ballot0 / 15

Fifteen lines Scarface, Jdub, Neto, Lauren, Mamba or Hayden state and you never have, quoted in their own words and ordered by how much each would move the engine. No charts, and it is the fastest section on the page — every yes here becomes work while you sleep, so it goes first.

01RULE 1Netosaid 3×
“the Retest on a level is never to the penny, is always close to the line”— Neto

What it would change: A retest touch has no stated tolerance in the code. Your 25%-of-the-previous-candle unit already governs the entry trigger, the 84% reclaim and stop slippage. This would be its fourth use, and it is nearly free.

Is this a rule of yours?

Nothing here becomes code without a yes.

02RULE 2Scarfacesaid 2×
“the reclaim entry is stopping us from trading chop… we should only trade a strong closure above that level, anything below is chop”— Scarface

What it would change: A different anchor for the level-not-respected downgrade — your highest-tripping one, which has failed three implementations. Chop measured by the strength of the breaking close, not by the bars after it.

Is this a rule of yours?

Nothing here becomes code without a yes.

03RULE 3Netosaid 7×
“a break, then displacement, then the retest, and lastly strong reaction on the key level — wait for how price reacts to your interest levels”— Neto

What it would change: Adds a fourth required element after the retest. The engine enters ON the retest; this would make it wait for the reaction to it.

Is this a rule of yours?

Nothing here becomes code without a yes.

04RULE 4Scarfacesaid 4×
“Ideally if you want to take a trade intraday you need this to break to hod or lod”— Scarface

What it would change: Target availability as an ENTRY gate. This is your own line — “if there are no other levels to target it is harder to trade” — stated as a hard precondition instead of a preference.

Is this a rule of yours?

Nothing here becomes code without a yes.

05RULE 5Netosaid 3×
“backtest and define if it works better for your ticker on the Pre Market levels, Previous Day levels, 1min/5min ORB”— Neto

What it would change: Your six levels are closed and applied to every symbol equally. This says the WEIGHTING among them should be per-ticker. Cheap to measure.

Is this a rule of yours?

Nothing here becomes code without a yes.

06RULE 6Netosaid 2×
“If reward potential is smaller, I'll usually secure profits more aggressively”— Neto

What it would change: Unparks your own scale-out question — “30 percent is when better chance stock runs, 50 for choppier, we must identify this”. He names the discriminator: how much reward is available at entry.

Is this a rule of yours?

Nothing here becomes code without a yes.

07RULE 7Lauren, Mamba and Jdubsaid 13×
“weekly, daily, 4H to identify the overall trend, key levels and liquidity zones — it needs to be paired with market conditions and HTF trend”— Lauren, Mamba and Jdub

What it would change: You said “you'll need to tell me what that is then”. Three mentors answer. Section 4 above is the measured version of this question; this line is whether it becomes a rule at all.

Is this a rule of yours?

Nothing here becomes code without a yes.

“Highest probability trades are always generally outside of previous days ranges or above/below key levels”— Hayden

What it would change: A prior-day-range containment filter. Computable at 9:29, and it joins the premarket filter that already ships.

Is this a rule of yours?

Nothing here becomes code without a yes.

09RULE 9Netosaid 3×

What it would change: A named shape for the retest candle. You have said trends respect wicky candles better; you never named the shape.

Is this a rule of yours?

Nothing here becomes code without a yes.

10RULE 10Mambasaid 2×
“I use op (the opening price) when there's no level or the level is too far, so it gives me a reference point”— Mamba
